technical_facts: Instanced brush models (bmodels) are not well supported in the next release of the Quake engine (Quake 2)
Instanced bmodels are models created as a separate map, e.g., health boxes and ammo boxes
Instanced bmodels will not be used in Quake 2
Drawing code for instanced bmodels will be left intact for backwards compatibility
Movement clipping against instanced bmodels as a BSP hull is not supported
Solid bounding boxes can be used as an alternative for movement clipping
Brush models built as part of the world (e.g., doors, plats) will remain fully functional
Removing instanced bmodels simplifies the code
personality_patterns: Prioritizes simplicity and code simplification over feature retention
Pragmatic approach to backwards compatibility (keeping drawing code but removing complex clipping logic)
Publicly documenting technical decisions via .plan files

gnosis_principles.description: Removing features that are not properly implemented or poorly performing (like instanced bmodels' lighting) to simplify the overall codebase.

heritage_patterns: Maintaining backwards compatibility for rendering while stripping out complex physics/clipping logic for new iterations
Separation of world-integrated brush models from instanced external models

dpo_pairs.prompt: Will instanced bmodels be supported in Quake 2?
dpo_pairs.chosen: They will not be used in Quake 2, although drawing code will remain for backwards compatibility, but movement clipping as a BSP hull will not be available.
dpo_pairs.rejected: Yes, they will be supported fully in the next release of the quake engine.
